title: Stratified prefill-decode allocator for phase-aware latency tiers
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: implement a stratified allocation policy that splits incoming requests into explicit latency tiers during prefill and decode and schedules GPU resources to meet latency SLOs while preserving overall throughput and fairness. Background: current prefill/decode arbiter applies a single-phase fairness model and frequently trades 95th P latency for bulk throughput under mixed workloads (small interactive chats + long batch completions). This ticket proposes: 1) classify requests into 3 runtime tiers (latency-critical, mixed, opportunistic) at scheduling time using request metadata and short historical latency profiles; 2) maintain separate soft-quotas and token budgets per tier but allow dynamic borrowing under low utilization; 3) integrate kernel selection hints (quantized vs FP16 kernels) and attention-optimizer compatibility into the estimator so the allocator is aware of per-request compute cost; 4) add a light-weight backlog estimator and token-cost predictor to decide when to move prefill tokens to an expedited decode fastpath (hedged decode) vs batching path. The design emphasizes graceful degradation: latency tiers get prioritized until quotas hit soft limits, after which weighted fairness applies across customers to avoid starvation.
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile latency for latency-critical tier reduced by >= 20% versus baseline workload mix in staging benchmarks
Overall throughput (tokens/sec) not reduced by more than 5% on standard mixed workload in staging
Per-customer fairness (weighted Jain index across active customers) >= 0.9 under synthetic adversarial mix (30% latency-critical from single customer)
Canary rollout with traffic split (5% -> 25% -> 100%) works without user-visible errors and metrics dashboards track tier adoption
Unit cost (GPU token cost estimate) for mixed workload improved or unchanged compared to baseline for >= 80% of traces
proposed_solution: Introduce a stratified allocator module that runs during admission before prefill scheduling. It will: 1) compute a tier score with a simple rule-based model (request latency tag, model, expected token length, customer SLA flag), 2) consult a short-term token-cost predictor that combines historical per-sequence kernel runtime and attention cost estimate, 3) assign requests to latency tiers and update soft-quotas stored in the scheduler state, 4) schedule work into existing prefill/decode pipelines but prefer hedged fastpath and small-batch kernels for latency-critical tier and use larger batching kernels for opportunistic tier. The allocator exposes knobs: tier thresholds, soft-quota sizes, borrow window, and kernel-hint weights. Metric hooks: per-tier latency SLO meters, backlog estimator gauge, fairness score, and cost-per-token estimate.
design_decisions: Prefer simple deterministic tiering rules + a small learned fallback to avoid high variance from complex ML classifiers at admission time
Keep soft-quotas (time-decayed) instead of hard reservation to enable better bin-packing and higher utilization
Integrate kernel selection as a hint rather than a hard binding to allow runtime fallback when a kernel is unavailable
Use weighted fairness across customers with higher weight for customers with paid SLAs; default weight=1 for self-serve
Avoid per-request expensive attention-cost modeling; use a cached small set of per-model attention profiles and multiply by token length
implementation_notes: Add allocator component under runtime/scheduler/stratified_allocator.go (prototype branch: github: redwood-inference/inference-runtime/tree/feature/stratified-allocator)
Expose config via runtime flags and Console feature flag (console.feature.stratified_allocator) for controlled rollout
Create a small in-memory token-cost cache with LRU eviction keyed by (model, quantization, seq_length_bin)
Instrument Grafana dashboard panel: dashboards/runtime/stratified-allocator to surface tier latencies, backlog, and fairness index
Unit tests: synthetic workload harness to assert scheduling decisions; integration test in ci-staging with mixed load generator
Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Stratified+Prefill-Decode+Allocator (internal design, decision log, simulation traces)
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable allocator in staging for 5% production-like traffic, monitor 95th latency & fairness for 48h
Phase 2 (gradual): 5% -> 25% -> 50% over 7 days with automated rollback if 95th latency regresses by >10% or fairness < 0.85
Phase 3 (full): enable for 100% when metrics stable and cost regression <5% for 72h
Fallback: runtime flag to disable stratified logic and revert to baseline arbiter; auto-fallback on memory pressure or missing kernel compatibility
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: misclassification of requests leads to throughput loss. Mitigation: allow immediate borrowing across tiers under low utilization and conservative default thresholds
Risk: increased scheduler complexity increases CPU overhead. Mitigation: keep admission logic O(1) per request and cache decisions for short windows (500ms)
Risk: interaction with kernel selection might cause unavailable fastpath. Mitigation: allocator treats kernel hints as best-effort and has a fallback path that retries with compatible kernels
Risk: fairness attacks by customer spamming short latency-critical requests. Mitigation: rate-limit per-customer on latency tier and enforce weighted fairness budget
